name: Enabling
overview: Scripture teaches that enabling others involves a responsible use of one's power to do good, as Proverbs 3:27 urges withholding no good when it is within one’s hand to give. Diligence and active effort are commended, with Proverbs 10:4 contrasting the poverty of slack hands against the wealth made by the diligent. At the same time, believers are called to personal responsibility, bearing their own burdens as Galatians 6:5 instructs, and to reject complicity with sin, avoiding fellowship with unfruitful works of darkness as Ephesians 5:11 commands. True freedom comes through knowing and living in the truth (John 8:32), which includes recognizing the judgment due to sin (Romans 1:32) and not taking pleasure in those who commit it.
